verdict: PARTIAL: the granulation chain is reproducible (isolation -> singleton/small ball -> del_ball minority loss -> sparse heterogeneous support). The last hop to poor classification is NOT supported: isolating-split rate does not correlate with Topo Delta Macro F1 and is essentially the same in adversarial vs informative R_opp runs. Do not modify the splitter for classifier gain yet. The repair below is justified only as a future granulation experiment whose success metric should be minority survival / small-ball rate, not Topo F1.
proposal: Smallest change, still KMeans(k=2), still rho=0.95, no downstream edits: after `split_2balls` assignment, repair only isolating children. If a child is small (n<=5) or singleton, carries the parent's local minority, and those points have heterogeneous support in the parent (n_opp_within_2*hd1 >= 2), reassign them to the sibling cluster. Leave unrepaired: (i) n_opp_within_2*hd1 == 1 outliers with large hd1_norm, (ii) mixed preserving splits. If repair would empty a child, skip that repair and keep the frozen KMeans partition. This keeps legitimate boundary minority inside a ball that survives del_ball, without changing KMeans(k=2), purity threshold, or GBLSTSVM. Implementation is deferred until a granulation-only replay is approved; do not screen GBLSTSVM yet.

definitions.global_minority: rarer class on the training split after normalize_labels
definitions.minority_isolating: one child is small (n<=5), pure, and contains all parent global-minority samples; sibling has none
definitions.minority_preserving: both children contain at least one global-minority sample
definitions.local_opp_support: mean # opposite-class parent samples within 2*hd1 of a minority point
definitions.survival: fraction of class samples whose leaf has n >= min_ball_count
